neighbours.label: next-word prediction of 'portion(s)' / 'serving(s)': fires on the token just before an expected portion or serving-size word in food and diet text (also 'Torah portion')
fire: Cheese is rich in fat, so pay attention to your serving size.
If you want to lose weight, start by cutting down your portions at dinner.
A smaller plate is a simple trick to help you manage portion sizes.
Pasta is fine in moderation as long as you watch your portions.
Dietitians say most restaurant meals contain two or three servings of grains.
Dried fruit is healthy, but measure out a single serving before you snack.
Each week the rabbi gives a talk on the weekly Torah portion after prayers.
The label lists calories per serving, so check how many servings are in the bag.
quiet: Cheese is rich in flavour, so pair it with a crisp white wine.
If you want to bake bread, start by warming the milk and the yeast.
A sharper knife is a simple trick to help you slice tomatoes thinly.
Pasta is best when the water is salted and boiling hard.
Chefs say most restaurant kitchens buy their vegetables from local markets.
Dried fruit is sweet, and it keeps for months in a sealed jar.
Each week the rabbi gives a talk on local history after prayers.
The label lists the country of origin and the date the coffee was roasted.

notes: The pole's output suppresses ' portion', ' portions', ' servings' on the + side, so the - pole promotes them. Probes: 'keep an eye on your serving size' 0.82, 'control your portions' 0.72, 'Torah portion' 0.63; 'A large portion of the budget' 0.00, 'four cloves of garlic' 0.06. It fires before the word, so a near miss sharing the lead-in also fired (0.82, 0.45); the near misses here use different lead-ins.
